1882.title: Jigoro Kano Founds Judo
1882.description: Jigoro Kano (1860–1938) founds the Kodokan in Tokyo and creates judo as a modern martial art, derived from traditional jiu-jitsu. The principle of "maximum efficiency, mutual welfare and benefit" becomes the heart of judo. He transformed the samurai fighting arts into a path of physical and spiritual development.

Jaren '20.title: Kawaishi Brings Judo to Europe
Jaren '20.description: Mikinosuke Kawaishi (1899–1969), a Japanese judo master, settles in Paris and revolutionises judo in Europe. He introduces the coloured belt system (white → yellow → orange → green → blue → brown → black) that is used the world over. He co-founded the French Judo Federation with Moshe Feldenkrais and created the Kawaishi Cup — the first international judo tournament between nations.

1956.title: Michigami Arrives in the Netherlands
1956.description: Haku Michigami (1912–2002), a Japanese judo master with an unbeaten competition record, becomes technical adviser to the Koninklijke Nederlandse Judobond. He stays in the Netherlands for 13 years and becomes Anton Geesink's personal trainer. He sent Geesink to the first international championship in Japan with the words: "Go and soak up the atmosphere."

Jaren '60.title: The Anton Geesink Era
Jaren '60.description: Anton Geesink (1929–2010), a pupil of Haku Michigami, becomes the first non-Japanese world judo champion (Paris, 1961). His Olympic gold in Tokyo (1964) makes judo popular in the Netherlands and Europe. Japanese spectators were so moved by his humble bow after the bout that judo enjoyed a new wave of popularity in both Japan and the Netherlands.

1976.title: Founding of OVJV
1976.description: Judovereniging OVJV (Oud-Vossemeerse Judo Vereniging) is founded — an independent judo club in Oud-Vossemeer. In 2026 OVJV celebrates its 50th anniversary and merges with Michigami.

Jaren '80.title: Koos van Wezel Teaches
Jaren '80.description: Before Judoclub Michigami existed, Koos van Wezel — a pupil of Haku Michigami — was already teaching judo with great passion at various locations in the region, including Tholen, Roosendaal and Scherpenisse.

1988.title: Wendy Jansen Starts Judo
1988.description: Wendy Jansen earns her white belt under Koos van Wezel in Tholen. She remains active for years, also after the founding of Michigami, and ultimately trains for her black belt.

1993.title: Founding of Judoclub Michigami
1993.description: Building on his experience as a coach, Koos van Wezel, his son Erwin van Wezel and Marinus Smout found Judoclub Michigami — officially established in Nieuw-Vossemeer, with the dojo in Sportcentrum De Knotwilg in Steenbergen. The name is a tribute to teacher Haku Michigami — master also of Anton Geesink.

Jaren '90 — 2000.title: Michigami's Golden Years
Jaren '90 — 2000.description: The club's golden age — the nineties and the noughties alike: two training groups on Thursdays, three groups on Fridays. Lessons in Nieuw-Vossemeer and Scherpenisse. Tournaments in London and Paris every year. Pony Park Slagharen with lessons from Anton Geesink himself. A true family club: son Erwin is active himself and teaches from time to time, Els always supports the club, and daughter Jolanda is a constant presence. Jolanda marries Franco Hack; together they have three sons, among them the twins Robin and Pascal — the two small judoka who will later become the board and coaches of Michigami. And then there is Alex van Loon, who assists Koos at training for years — an indispensable second hand behind the mat.
Jaren '90 — 2000.photoCaption: Annual training camp in Slagharen — photographed with Anton Geesink

2010.title: Robin, Pascal & Robert Earn 1st Dan
2010.description: On 5 June 2010 the new generation — Robin Hack, Pascal Hack and Robert Dingenouts — all three pass their 1st Dan black belt. A milestone for three friends who have practised judo together since almost the club's founding.

2014.title: Robin, Pascal & Robert Earn 2nd Dan
2014.description: On 7 June 2014 Robin Hack, Pascal Hack and Robert Dingenouts jointly earn their 2nd Dan black belt. A fine milestone in their long judo journey.
2014.photoCaption: After passing the 2nd Dan — from left to right: Robert, Pascal, Koos and Robin

2015.title: Dutch Open International Championships
2015.description: 4 judoka from Michigami take part in the Dutch Open in Dalfsen. Latif Nurzad, Ricardo den Heijer and Damian van Leijenhorst all finish second — a respectable achievement at national level.

2016.title: Robin, Pascal & Robert Earn 3rd Dan
2016.description: On 4 June 2016 the trio passes its 3rd Dan black belt. A high level that testifies to years of dedication to the sport.

2018.title: 25th Anniversary
2018.description: Judoclub Michigami celebrates its 25th anniversary with a major tournament on 6 October — a day full of judo, prizes and gratitude for all the volunteers and members.

Jaren '10.title: Gradual Decline & the Coronavirus Crisis
Jaren '10.description: From the mid-2010s things gradually grow quieter: there are fewer competition judoka, which makes tournaments harder to organise, the membership shrinks and clubs disappear from the region. The coronavirus crisis (2020–2021) is then the final blow: many clubs go under, and Michigami barely stays on its feet. Afterwards the club works hard to grow and improve again.

2021.title: Full Takeover After Koos's Passing
2021.description: Koos van Wezel dies in December 2021 at far too young an age. Robin, Pascal and Robert — who had been teaching alongside Koos for years — take full charge of the club and ensure that the spirit of Michigami lives on.

2024.title: Development & Independence
2024.description: New mats (120 m²), Chiem and Jacco pass their 1st Dan. First open Club Championship with OVJV, Yoshi and Judo Edegem. CJJF membership ended — the club continues independently.

2024b.title: Wendy Jansen Earns 1st Dan
2024b.description: After a long absence at brown-belt level, Wendy returns and in 2024 earns her 1st Dan black belt. She now teaches in both Oud-Vossemeer and Steenbergen and is responsible for first aid.

2026.title: Minute of Silence for Franco Hack (1966–2026)
2026.description: On 28 March, Franco Hack — fourth dan, father of Robin and Pascal, Koos's son-in-law — dies at just 59 years of age. He trained many members on their way to their black belt, practised kata's with them and served as uke for several judoka at dan examinations. He was a wonderful sparring partner, especially in ne-waza, sat with Jolanda behind the jury table at countless tournaments, and was coach on international outings such as the CSIT in Grenoble. On 1 April the club observes a minute of silence for him in Steenbergen and Oud-Vossemeer — seated around the mat, together.
2026.photoCaption: 1 April 2026 · minute of silence for Franco Hack, De Vossenkuil Oud-Vossemeer

2026b.title: OVJV Takeover & 50th Anniversary
2026b.description: Michigami takes over OVJV (Oud-Vossemeerse Judo Vereniging) in a transition year. OVJV celebrates its 50th anniversary with a tournament in October. From 2027: two locations, one club.

Vandaag.title: Michigami Today
Vandaag.description: Judoclub Michigami trains at De Knotwilg (Steenbergen) and De Vossenkuil (Oud-Vossemeer). Two age groups, recreational and competitive — from toddlers to adults. With its own teaching system that combines three traditions.
